neighbours.label: The split-off ending piece where 'e' meets another vowel (-ea, -ée, -ae, -eus, -eo) at the end of a longer proper name: Medea, Nicaea, Hosea, Galatea, Elysée, Renée, Désirée, Mycenae, Philae, Odysseus, Orfeo. Second trigger: the garden word allée(s). Quiet for short names (Thea, Lea, Bea), names ending without that 'e' (Lavinia, Samoa, Joshua, Daphne, Penelope), names that are one whole token (Korea, Athena, Crimea), and ordinary words with the same ending (fiancée, idée, nausea, antennae, algae).
neighbours.short: 'e'+vowel ending piece of a longer name (Med-ea, Elys-ée, Mycen-ae)
fire: In the tragedy, Medea takes a terrible revenge on Jason.
The bishops gathered at Nicaea in the year 325.
The prophet Hosea compared the nation to an unfaithful spouse.
Pygmalion carved a statue that later came to be called Galatea.
The president received the delegation at the Élysée Palace.
Her grandmother Renée still bakes bread every Sunday.
Désirée opened the café on the corner last spring.
Archaeologists uncovered the Lion Gate at Mycenae.
quiet: In the tragedy, Lavinia takes a terrible revenge on her enemies.
The bishops gathered at Rome in the year 325.
The prophet Joshua led the nation across the river.
Apollo chased a nymph who later came to be called Daphne.
The president received the delegation at the palace in Seoul, Korea.
Her grandmother Thea still bakes bread every Sunday.
Penelope opened the café on the corner last spring.
Archaeologists uncovered an ancient wall near Athena's shrine in Crimea.
